name: BAŚKA
description: Baśka (pronounced 'Bash-ka') is a distinctively fast-paced, 16-card trick-taking game from the Kashubian region of northern Poland. A member of the Schafkopf family, it is played with just the highest honors from a standard deck (A, 10, Q, J). The game is celebrated for its secret partnerships determined by the possession of 'Old Ones' (Black Queens) and its high-stakes solo bids.

content.text: Baśka (pronounced 'Bash-ka') is a distinctively fast-paced, 16-card trick-taking game from the Kashubian region of northern Poland. A member of the Schafkopf family, it is played with just the highest honors from a standard deck (A, 10, Q, J). The game is celebrated for its secret partnerships determined by the possession of 'Old Ones' (Black Queens) and its high-stakes solo bids.

Developed in the Kashubian communities along the Baltic Sea. It is an adaptation of the German game 'Kop' (Head), which itself is a simplified version of Schafkopf. The name 'Baśka' is a Kashubian diminutive for 'Barbara'.
4 players. Two are 'The Old Ones' (holders of Black Queens) and two are the opponents.
16 cards: Ace, 10, Queen, and Jack of each suit.
16-card specific pack or a stripped 52-card deck (keep A, 10, Q, J only).
Each player is dealt 4 cards (usually 2 and 2).

items.text: Bez Atu: A variation where only Aces and Tens are points, and no trumps exist (very rare).
Silent Zolo: A player plays solo without announcing it until the first trick is played.
